latest_pilot.queue_case: 16 nodes, 1 block, 32 threads, zero body, five repetitions per process
latest_pilot.observer_control: host timing plus per-enqueue error queries disabled for both arms
latest_pilot.reason: The two orderings disagree and the ABBA estimate exceeds the 2% perturbation budget; current desktop/GPU load is not a quiet baseline.
diagnostic_findings: In a reduced five-configuration launch-gap diagnostic, replay uncovered gaps were materially below ordinary gaps but varied with geometry, body, and dependency mode.
This supports separate mode and geometry features; it does not justify one global graph scalar.

objective: Separate host submission, driver/device dispatch, graph replay, and physical kernel/memory work, then test a cheap graph-on/off residual model on independent holdouts.
completion_conditions: Every enabled parameter has a named hardware/runtime scope and an independent holdout result.
No holdout prediction uses that sample's measured kernel duration or LLM latency as an input.
The simulator's default path meets the runtime budget and preserves physical work, bytes, energy, and dependencies.
A graph scalar is marked qualified only after all measurement and performance gates pass; otherwise it remains diagnostic sensitivity data.
non_goals: No universal CUDA Graph constant is inferred from one RTX 5080/Windows observation.
No empirical observer penalty is subtracted from a timed result.
No full Cartesian product of node counts, geometries, payloads, bodies, and graph modes is required.
No native LLM latency is used to fit a synthetic dispatch parameter.

simulation_runtime.new_event_budget: at most one compact packet update per batch, plus at most two milestone updates per PDL edge
simulation_runtime.scope_note: These relaxed limits apply only to simulator runtime and memory overhead. Measurement perturbation and predictive accuracy gates remain unchanged.

measurement.run_order: balanced ABBA/BAAB within each block; randomize block order with a recorded seed
measurement.quietness: record CPU/GPU load and clocks outside the timed region; do not claim a quiet baseline from one nvidia-smi snapshot
measurement.clock_rule: do not subtract CPU and GPU timestamps without a validated clock bridge

generalization.holdout_split: never used for fitting, threshold selection, or relabeling
generalization.out_of_domain: fall back to the existing model and mark the audit partial

current_environment_snapshot.note: The utilization value is only a preflight snapshot; it is not a calibration datum.

desktop_isolation_gate.reason: Both monitors are currently attached to the RTX display path; selecting AMD in an application preference cannot move the desktop compositor.
desktop_isolation_gate.user_hardware_action: Move the monitor cables from the RTX 5080 outputs to the motherboard video outputs, then boot or reconnect the displays. This cannot be completed through the repository or software alone.
pass_checks: dxdiag reports a real current mode for AMD Radeon(TM) Graphics and no active desktop mode for NVIDIA
dwm.exe is absent from the NVIDIA GPU Engine counters for three consecutive samples
nvidia-smi utilization remains 0% for at least 30 seconds with no calibration process running
desktop_isolation_gate.fallback: If the motherboard outputs are unavailable, keep the current topology and mark calibration as non-quiet; do not claim the RTX is idle.

host_submission.boundary: CPU API enqueue begin/end and release
limitations: The default probe calls cudaPeekAtLastError on every enqueue; P0 controls can disable this with --check-errors 0.
Therefore it does not represent natural streaming supply and cannot establish that all WDDM commands are resident when the gate opens.

device_dispatch.boundary: signed uncovered gaps between effective kernel body envelopes; first-node dispatch is unobserved
device_dispatch.status: diagnostic_until_body, entry, exit, and PDL completion tails are separated
rules: Do not add body duration, device span, or memory traffic to dispatch residuals.
Keep negative signed gaps as a diagnostic; never convert them to negative task demand.
Measure ordinary, graph first, uploaded first, and replay as separate modes.

typed_activity.boundary: CUPTI kernel/copy activity identity and count validation
typed_activity.status: observer-on results are perturbation diagnostics until paired with observer-off runs
typed_activity.rule: Never use an activity-observer overhead ratio as a correction factor.

llm_end_to_end.boundary: serial native and simulator TTFT, TPOT, and E2E for the same physical task shape
llm_end_to_end.tool: existing native benchmark and graph validation path
llm_end_to_end.status: final validation only; never a calibration input
llm_end_to_end.rule: Use new model parameters only after synthetic train/holdout gates pass.

phases.name: capability_and_perturbation_pilot
phases.purpose: Verify what each probe actually observes before collecting calibration data.
actions: Run build-only checks for the launch-gap, queue, typed-activity, and graph-structure probes.
Run the ETW access check as an optional capability probe; permission failure is recorded and does not block the synthetic path.
Add a probe-level observer toggle for host timestamps, per-launch error queries, CUPTI, and flush/tail queries. Keep buffers preallocated and keep logging outside the timed region.
For each of three short cases, collect paired observer-off/on blocks in ABBA and BAAB order with the same warmups.
pass: Paired median observer effect is at most 2% or the declared timing resolution, whichever is larger.
If this fails, observer-on data stays diagnostic and no correction is applied.
phases.deliverable: capability.json plus raw paired samples; no production parameter

phases.name: synthetic_train
phases.purpose: Identify only the low-dimensional residual terms that are distinguishable from physical work.
phases.budget: At most 24 configurations x 11 repetitions; no full Cartesian sweep.
rules: Fit host submission, device dispatch, and graph replay in separate columns.
Do not fix a 2048 ns quantum or a packet period until residuals demonstrate that it is stable across the train axes.
If intermediate payloads such as 160 or 544 bytes are needed, extend the CUDA probe explicitly; never map them to the nearest supported payload.

phases.name: synthetic_holdout
phases.purpose: Test generalization across unseen bodies, node counts, geometries, payloads, and ordering.
phases.budget: At most 16 configurations x 11 repetitions, selected before P1 fitting.

qualification.conditional_diagnostic_rule: A holdout prediction must use a body model from train or declared input, never that holdout's measured body span.

phases.name: source_shaped_and_end_to_end_validation
phases.purpose: Check that the residual model transfers to owned source dispatch shapes and then to short real serving requests.
source_shaped_cases: one unsupported hybrid topology as an explicit rejection case
rules: Keep native and simulator runs serial and paired; the previous 20-concurrent-job result is not a speed baseline.
Use native latency only for final validation and graph on/off direction, never for fitting.
Do not divide one physical kernel, copy, or DRAM demand by source-node count.
phases.promotion_target: Relative MAPE reduction of at least 10% versus the same simulator baseline, with no workload subgroup worsening by more than 2 percentage points; this is a promotion target, not a claim about current accuracy.

phases.name: cheap_simulator_integration
phases.purpose: Enable only a compact residual lookup/interpolator whose runtime cost is bounded.
implementation: Store one immutable compact descriptor per compiled graph structure and reuse the existing bounded template cache (maximum 8).
Keep per-stream state to next packet, credit count, and last completion point; update it in O(1) per dispatch.
Reuse existing task, byte, energy, work, and dependency objects. Attach one compact audit reference per invocation instead of copying a full DAG per event.
Take the existing fast path when no in-domain qualified profile is present; do not profile with NVML or scan a full graph during simulation.
For an out-of-domain or unqualified profile, retain the current analytical cost and mark the audit partial.
phases.promotion_gate: All P0-P3 gates plus the simulation runtime and memory gates in guardrails must pass on serial paired runs.

execution_order: Create a new output directory; never overwrite existing raw measurements.
Run P0 build/capability checks and record tool, device, driver, runtime, OS, and git revision.
Run P0 observer pairs; stop promotion if observer perturbation is not bounded.
Freeze the P1/P2 case roles and seed in the plan before collecting any P1 result.
Collect P1 train only, fit a scoped residual model, then collect untouched P2 holdouts.
Run P3 source-shaped and serial LLM checks; compare against the unchanged simulator baseline.
Run P4 overhead checks with the new logic disabled and enabled on the same inputs.
Only then write a profile with graph_device_launch_qualified=true; otherwise keep the value false.

existing_tool_commands.warning: The queue runner is preloaded-gate and supports payload extras 0/64/160/256/544/1024, including the explicit P2 holdouts 160 and 544. The paired observer runner records ABBA/BAAB blocks but does not promote results automatically. The compiled queue executable supports --host-timing-mode total for low-perturbation aggregate host timing; per-node timing and device-gated samples remain diagnostic until P0 passes.

stop_rules: Stop promotion if a holdout is fitted, relabeled, or fed its measured body duration.
Stop promotion if host and device costs are added for the same physical work owner.
Stop promotion if default simulation overhead exceeds 10% median, enabled overhead exceeds 10% median, or tail overhead exceeds 10%.
Stop promotion if graph on/off changes physical bytes, energy, work, or dependency ownership without an independent physical explanation.
Stop and report partial if the probe cannot distinguish first-node dispatch, PDL completion, or observer-induced work.
